newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-CATT OMISSION NO SURPRISE, SAYS DU PLESSIS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CATT OMISSION NO SURPRISE, SAYS DU PLESSIS.

text.p: Springbok coach Carel du Plessis believes the Lions selectors were correct to omit South African-born fly-half Mike Catt from the British Isles squad to tour the Republic in May and June.
Catt had played himself into contention for a tour berth wearing England's number 10 jersey at the end of the Five Nations championship.
But he was left out in favour of Scotland's Gregor Townsend and England team-mate Paul Grayson when the 35-man squad was announced in London on Wednesday.
"He wasn't at the level one should expect from a test player and I have to say I wasn't surprised at his omission," said du Plessis on Thursday.

"There were one or two new names in the squad but no major shocks. I thought we might see Jonathan Davies in there - he is an attacking fly-half, a playmaker, but in Gregor Townsend they have a player with the same sort of ability."

Du Plessis was appointed Springbok coach in February following the resignation in disgrace of Andre Markgraaff after the broadcast of a tape-recorded conversation in which he insulted senior black figures in the South African game.
Du Plessis will not name his first squad of 21 until June 2 -- they have a warm-up test against Tonga at Newlands on June 10 -- but can now assess the Lions' hand.
"It's a well-balanced squad," he said. "There's two good teams in there with the midweek team well matched with the likely test side.
"But it will be interesting to see what combinations they put together.
"The pack is heavy and strong with good ball-winners and line-out men, while the backline has been beefed up defensively with some of the rugby league players who have returned to rugby union.
"I'm quite interested to see how they work out their fly-half, full-back and wing combinations though.
"If they have Gregor Townsend at fly-half, do they have Neil Jenkins at full-back? He is a reliable place-kicker but is he going to make it as the test full-back?"

The Lions play three tests against the Springboks as well as 10 matches against provincial sides including games against all four of South Africa's representatives in the cauldron of the southern hemisphere Super 12 competition.
"There is seen to be a gap between the northern and southern hemisphere games but I have seen a change in the Five Nations this year," added du Plessis.
"It's about pace, physical presence and sharpening up their skills and you can see they have tried to change but everything is not quite in place yet.
"We don't underestimate the Lions. They are coming here to prove a point but we will be ready for them."
The Lions start their tour with a match against Eastern Province in Port Elizabeth on May 24. The first test is in Cape Town on June 21.
